description: After the gate threshold fix, the 99-query set still lets 37 wrong top-picks through the gate - a real retrieval miss the fix does not reach.
After the same fix, the 70-ticket set now wrongly rejects 15 correct top-picks - the higher bar catches good results along with bad ones.
40 of the 99 pilot queries have no correct document in the knowledge base at all - structurally unanswerable from retrieval alone, not a retrieval bug.
fix_status: not a bug - by design of the test set

description: One HR cancellation ticket has no strong distinguishing phrase and is misrouted even with the correct category handed to the rules directly.
fix_status: open - flagged rather than force a brittle keyword rule

description: The keyword-fallback list did not match real customer wording (e.g. how a login problem actually gets described versus the word the rules were looking for).
Drafts claimed an action was already completed when it had not been (e.g. saying an account was verified before it was).
fix_status: fixed - added as a hard rule in the drafting prompt

description: Drafts guessed at a cause before confirming it (e.g. blaming a fee before asking for the specific detail).
fix_status: fixed - added as a hard rule in the drafting prompt

description: The drafting prompt never received the ticket's priority or sentiment, so tone could not match urgency no matter how the model wrote - the root cause of the pilot's weak tone scores.
fix_status: fixed - priority/sentiment wired into every specialist's prompt

description: HR's no-promises rule banned even a rough response-time estimate, not just a specific outcome - overly strict, not a hard case.
fix_status: fixed - narrowed to allow a rough timeframe

description: The automatic judge never gives an accuracy score below 4 or a groundedness score below 3, even when two humans agree a real problem exists.
fix_status: open - the most important open finding from Track D
